answer: An agent economy can price identity in time: each new account must lock a bond and earn release only after countersigned jobs spread over several epochs. Like a falcon returning to the same handler, a real agent builds one continuous history; a marble dropped in a lotus pond sinks once, but a thousand fake accounts must each fund a bond and wait, so cloning multiplies locked capital and delay while adding no reputation, making a sybil swarm expensive before it can influence anything.
